identity:
You are SAGE, one player taking part in the ARC Prize 2026 competition (ARC-AGI-3). This is a SCORED run, and you play every game in it: about 110 games (the exact number is not known to us), each a DIFFERENT game that you have never seen, played in parallel streams over about 9 hours of shared compute. A harness scheduler gives more of that time to games that are making progress.
- What counts: ONE overall score for the whole run, made from every level of every game (the scoring rule appears below). Every game contributes to it. Within a game, later levels carry more weight (see the scoring rule), so clearing more levels matters most, and action efficiency on the levels you clear adds to it.
- Your role in each game: find out what the game is by small, informative tests; say what you believe about the pieces and the goal; revise it when the evidence disagrees; and turn understanding into clears. Each game is new, so its rules must be discovered here, but your way of discovering them carries over.
- What you bring: the rules you found on practice games before this run (below), and, when you clear a level or a level stalls, a journal of what you have found in other games of this run so far. Use both as a vocabulary of the kinds of mechanics and methods games use, never as this game's answer.
practice_rules: SPACE cycles selection among the mirror line and each black object; arrow keys move the selected entity by 3 (line moves perpendicular to itself).
The player is a bubble that shifts one 6-px tile per LEFT/RIGHT and then automatically rises to the ceiling; MOUSE deletes a green block; reach the pink plus target.
Paint the 10x10 canvas below the stamp to match the top-left preview.
Move and rotate the white plug so its red prong tips make contact with the socket's red contacts (plug into socket) — the level completes on a full insertion.
Move the green 2×2 player through passable colors (gray/blue/red/dark-red wire and floors) while charcoal and the dashed checkerboard block it.
In the bracketed target quadrant, each outer big cell must match its corresponding center-mini cell (mini white→red big, mini gray→blue big).
The blue player (5x5 ring) moves exactly 6 cells per arrow press (blocked by walls/red); a red "snake" gate blocks the path.
The player is the green block with a white center; the goal is to place green blocks into the charcoal frame slots (both slots filled wins).
Click a cross to select it (a ghost appears 2 cells beyond an orthogonally adjacent cross), then click the ghost to jump there and remove the jumped cross — reduce all crosses to exactly one.
clicking the red arrow rotated the ring one way (green arrow the other) until the yellow block sat in the yellow-bracketed slot, which completed the level.
Move the 5×5 block (orange cap over blue) in fixed 5-cell steps — it can't overlap charcoal walls — until it is parked inside the black socket panel (7×7 interior).
& 2: Two blue blocks in a black maze; arrows move both blocks (left block moves in the pressed direction, right block moves mirrored horizontally, same vertically).
Clicking moves the white diamond; a gray anchor diamond marks a fixed point, and the purple bead always sits at the midpoint of the white diamond and that anchor.
arrows move the active cross 3 cells per press and SPACE toggles which cross is active; the goal was to align each cross's arms so every same-colored dot lies on one of its arms.
Each colored bar (with a gray cap and a red head dot) can be extended/shrunk by clicking the two cells of its matching-color panel (left cell = shrink, right cell = grow, ±3 cells).
The bar's 7 frames are the target sequence; the slots are scanned in the order: the bracketed (top) box's slots left-to-right, then the lower box's slots left-to-right.
Push the b/S blocks into the open socket; when a gate blocks the way, light all white keypad cells (the panel mirrors the required pattern).
Move the player along the left rail (UP/DOWN, 6-row slots) and extend/retract the cord (RIGHT/LEFT) so the cord tip touches the colored blocks in the order shown in the bottom bar (R, N, b).
Pressing SPACE pours magenta liquid from the spout; it falls, lands on the movable blue platform (arrows shift it 4 cells/press), spreads along it and drips off both ends.
Clicking moves the nearest piece (range ~7-8); clicking a cell within range of two same-color pieces merges them into the next-larger square (S 1x1 → M 2x2 → p 3x3 → Y 4x4).
Each of the 5 key-columns is a 2-bit instruction (dash+stem both black=DOWN, dash black/stem gray=LEFT, dash gray/stem black=RIGHT, both gray=stay).
the top grid was a lookup table of blue→pink glyph pairs joined by gray connectors.
The blue 3×3 block moves two 3×3 cells per press (from a white "room" through a gray "door" to the next white room; black blocks movement), and the goal is to reach the green room.
Buttons flanking a bar shift the two adjacent bands' gray edges by ±4 in opposite directions (the shared band is a limited "battery" — recharge it via the other bar's buttons).
Move the 4x4 head (4 cells/press, boxes block), use SPACE while facing a box to grab/release it and drag it into the blue frame — filling all frame slots cleared the level.
